title: PATENT RESEARCH REPORT
abstract: This technical report synthesizes patent evidence for the preparation, polymerization, and copolymerization of Polycarbonate. Analyzing 15 primary patents, the report identifies key technical approaches including continuous melt polymerization, transition-metal-catalyzed copolymerization of carbon dioxide with epoxides (using cobalt-salen and bimetallic zinc catalysts), metal-free anionic copolymerization using phosphazene bases, and the synthesis of functional polycarbonates containing azido groups for biomedical hydrogels. Key process trends highlight a shift toward highly regioselective catalysts, metal-free systems for color-free solids, and precise control of end-group functionality (achieving up to 99% OH end groups) for polyol applications.

patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses a method of preparing polycarbonate terpolymers using monomers like BPA, hydroquinone, and methyl hydroquinone with PCP chainstoppers.

experimental_evidence: Terpolymer synthesis with 33% BPA, 34% hydroquinone, and 33% methyl hydroquinone.
Addition of para-cumyl phenol (PCP) chainstopper to yield 30, 50, or 70 mol% end groups at a target molecular weight of 30,000 g/mol.
Thermal processing zones set at 280°C, 290°C, and 300°C.
Ultrasonic treatment of the terpolymer for 15 minutes followed by shaking for 2 hours.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses a method of preparing polycarbonate terpolymers using monomers like BPA, hydroquinone, and methyl hydroquinone with PCP chainstoppers.

patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses continuous polymerization processes using vertical and horizontal stirring reactors to produce polycarbonates from isosorbide, tricyclodecanedimethanol, and diphenyl carbonate.

experimental_evidence: Continuous feed of molten starting materials through a pipe heated to 140°C into a vertical stirring reactor.
Polymerization initiated using cesium carbonate catalyst (0.2% aqueous solution).
Average residence time maintained at 60 minutes by regulating the polymer discharge line valve.
Resulting polycarbonates exhibit reduced viscosities of 0.55-0.60, Tg of 129°C, and 5% weight loss temperatures of 337-350°C.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses continuous polymerization processes using vertical and horizontal stirring reactors to produce polycarbonates from isosorbide, tricyclodecanedimethanol, and diphenyl carbonate.

patent_details.patent_title: Process of producing polycarbonate by copolymerization of carbon dioxide and …
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses copolymerization of carbon dioxide and epoxides (like propylene oxide) using cobalt-salen complexes to produce polycarbonates.

experimental_evidence: Copolymerization of carbon dioxide and propylene oxide in a 50 mL bomb reactor.
Catalyst complexes prepared using cobalt acetate and various salen ligands with high yields (up to 100%).
Continuous injection of carbon dioxide at 20 bar for 1 hour at 70-75°C.
Induction times vary significantly from 1 hour (dry winter conditions) to 12 hours (high-temperature, high-humidity summer conditions).
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses copolymerization of carbon dioxide and epoxides (like propylene oxide) using cobalt-salen complexes to produce polycarbonates.

patent_details.patent_title: Method of synthesising polycarbonates in the presence of a bimetallic catalyst …
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses synthesis of polycarbonates by copolymerizing carbon dioxide and cyclohexene oxide (CHO) using bimetallic zinc catalysts and chain transfer agents.

experimental_evidence: Copolymerization of CO2 and cyclohexene oxide (CHO) using bimetallic zinc catalysts ([L1Zn2(OAc)2] or [L1Zn2(CF3COO)2]).
Addition of chain transfer agents (A through Q) or water to produce polycyclohexene oxide carbonate polyols and diols.
High selectivity for copolymer formation (>99% carbonate linkages) maintained even in the presence of excess water.
Reaction mixtures quenched using a 5% solution of HCl/MeOH in dichloromethane.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses synthesis of polycarbonates by copolymerizing carbon dioxide and cyclohexene oxide (CHO) using bimetallic zinc catalysts and chain transfer agents.

patent_details.patent_title: Polycarbonate copolymer and method of producing the same
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses polycarbonate copolymers containing isosorbide, 1,4-CHDM, TCDDM, and other dihydroxy compounds with high thermal stability.

experimental_evidence: Synthesis of polycarbonate copolymers using isosorbide, tricyclodecanedimethanol (TCDDM), and other dihydroxy compounds.
Evaluation of thermal properties, including 5% weight reduction temperatures.
Comparison with commercial homopolymers (e.g., Iupilon H4000) and specific ternary copolymer compositions.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses polycarbonate copolymers containing isosorbide, 1,4-CHDM, TCDDM, and other dihydroxy compounds with high thermal stability.

patent_details.patent_title: Copolymerization of carbon dioxide and cyclic monomers to form polycarbonates
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses metal-free anionic copolymerization of carbon dioxide and cyclic monomers (epoxides) using phosphazene bases (t-BuP4) and diols.

experimental_evidence: Metal-free anionic copolymerization of epoxides (propylene oxide, cyclohexene oxide, etc.) with CO2.
Use of 1,4-benzyldimethanol (BDM) and t-BuP4 base to initiate perfectly alternating copolymerization.
Achieved molar masses up to 250,000 g/mol with narrow molecular weight distributions (Mw/Mn < 1.3).
Reactions quenched using HCl in methanol (1 mol/L) or 10% HCl.

patent_details.patent_title: Methods for producing polycarbonate copolymer and polysiloxane compound, …
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses preparation of polycarbonate-polysiloxane copolymers and polyarylene siloxanes.

experimental_evidence: Solidified reaction mixture treated with 20 g heptane, heated to 90°C, and subjected to hot filtration.
Crystals washed with cold heptane (5°C) and dried under reduced pressure (1 hPa) for 45 hours to yield white powders.
Colorless and transparent polyarylene siloxane obtained by heating under normal pressure over 1.5 hours.

patent_details.patent_title: Polyether polycarbonate diol and method for producing same
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses polyether polycarbonate diols and methods for their production.

experimental_evidence: Discloses synthesis and characterization of polyether polycarbonate diols.
Focuses on achieving specific diol structures for polyurethane applications.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses polyether polycarbonate diols and methods for their production.

patent_details.patent_title: Method of producing crystalline polycarbonate powders
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses a method for preparing partially crystalline polycarbonate powders with controlled particle size via precipitation.

experimental_evidence: Amorphous polycarbonate dissolved in dichloromethane (20 wt%) and gradually added to acetone (non-solvent) under high shear mixing (6000 rpm).
Resulting powder consists of ~93% particles with an average size of less than 150 μm.
Precipitated polycarbonate exhibits crystallinity between 20% and 35%.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses a method for preparing partially crystalline polycarbonate powders with controlled particle size via precipitation.

patent_details.patent_title: Polycarbonates made using highly selective catalysts
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses highly regioselective copolymerization of carbon dioxide and propylene oxide using cobalt-salen catalysts.

experimental_evidence: Copolymerization of neat propylene oxide and CO2 in a Parr autoclave using [(R,R)-(salen)CoOAc] or [(R,R)-(salen)CoBr] catalysts.
Achieved high carbonate linkages (>=98%) and high regioselectivity (80-85% head-to-tail).
Precipitation of yellow crude complex by adding water (150 mL) to the reaction mixture.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses highly regioselective copolymerization of carbon dioxide and propylene oxide using cobalt-salen catalysts.

patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses a method for quenching polymerization reactions of aliphatic polycarbonates using specific solvent mixtures.

experimental_evidence: Preparation of poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC) polymer in a pressurized reactor.
Dilution of the reaction mixture (dope) with propyl acetate to yield a composition of 50 wt% propyl acetate, 30 wt% propylene oxide, and 20 wt% PPC polymer.
Quenching process designed to stabilize the polymer and prevent degradation.

patent_details.patent_title: Monomers and polymers for functional polycarbonates and poly(ester-carbonates) …
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses functional cyclic carbonate monomers (like AzDXO) and their ring-opening polymerization to form functional polycarbonates.

experimental_evidence: Synthesis of azido-functionalized cyclic carbonate monomer (AzDXO) in two steps with 45.6% overall yield.
Ring-opening polymerization of AzDXO and copolymerization with L-lactide using DBU catalyst.
Rapid gellation (<1 min) of cell-hydrogel constructs via strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition (SPAAC) click reaction.
primary_patents.technical_relevance: Discloses functional cyclic carbonate monomers (like AzDXO) and their ring-opening polymerization to form functional polycarbonates.

patent_details.patent_title: Monomers and polymers for functional polycarbonates and poly (ester-carbonates) …
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses functional cyclic carbonate monomers (AzDXO) and polycarbonates for biomedical applications, detailing ROP kinetics.

experimental_evidence: Determination of ring-opening polymerization (ROP) rate constants for AzDXO (0.084 min^-1) and L-lactide (0.116 min^-1).
Synthesis of PEG-P(AzDXO) macromers with >95% overall yield.
Characterization of polymer crystallinity and glass transitions using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC).

patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses polycarbonate polyols with high OH end-group content prepared using cobalt catalysts and chain transfer agents.

experimental_evidence: Synthesis of polycarbonate polyols in a Fisher-Potter bottle or glass vessel under vacuum.
Copolymerization of propylene oxide and CO2 using cobalt catalysts (E1 or E2) and PPN+Cl- co-catalyst.
Use of chain transfer agents like 1,4-cyclohexanedimethanol, propoxylated pentaerythritol, succinic acid, or adipic acid to control molecular weight.
Resulting polyols contain 97% to 99% OH end groups.

patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses polycarbonate polyols with high OH end-group content prepared using cobalt catalysts and chain transfer agents (similar to US11535706).

experimental_evidence: Copolymerization of propylene oxide and CO2 using cobalt catalysts (E1 or E2) and PPN+Cl- co-catalyst.
Incorporation of starter diols/triols (e.g., 1,4-cyclohexanedimethanol, propoxylated pentaerythritol) to yield polyols with 97-99% OH end groups.
Reactions quenched with acid, diluted with acetone, and concentrated to yield crude polymer.

cross_patent_comparison: Transition-metal catalysts (cobalt-salen and bimetallic zinc) enable highly selective CO2/epoxide copolymerization at moderate temperatures (20-80 °C) but leave metal residues.

Metal-free anionic systems utilizing phosphazene bases (t-BuP4) or PPNCl/triethylborane complexes offer a clean alternative, yielding color-free solid polycarbonates with narrow molecular weight distributions.

Melt transesterification processes require high temperatures (up to 140 °C and above) and vacuum to drive the reaction, whereas copolymerization reactions run under elevated CO2 pressures (1 to 55 bar).
Functional polycarbonates prepared via ring-opening polymerization of azido-functionalized monomers (AzDXO) provide unique post-polymerization modification capabilities, stable up to 130 °C.
conclusion: The analyzed patent landscape for Polycarbonate reveals three dominant technical paradigms: high-temperature continuous melt transesterification for engineering thermoplastics, transition-metal or metal-free copolymerization of CO2 with cyclic ethers for aliphatic polycarbonates, and ring-opening polymerization of functional cyclic carbonates for biomedical applications. Key process trends emphasize the optimization of catalyst selectivity (achieving >99% carbonate linkages and high regioselectivity), the elimination of metal residues to produce color-free polymers, and the precise control of molecular weight and end-group functionality (97-99% OH end groups) for polyurethane prepolymers. Gaps in the patent evidence include detailed long-term aging and mechanical performance data for the resulting copolymers.
